metadata.title: zERC20 Privacy Token Protocol - Audit Map Batch 3
metadata.methodology: 5-phase attack vector analysis with counterexample construction

audit_results.title: Wrap operation atomicity verification

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Attempt to trigger wrap completion without successful underlying transfer
input_validation_bypass.analysis: The _wrap function performs: (1) balance check at line 255-264, (2) received validation at line 266, (3) reward calculation at 271-273, and (4) mint at 275. If underlying transfer fails, safeTransferFrom reverts. If received == 0, UnderlyingPullFailed() reverts. All operations are in single transaction with no intermediate saves.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Attempt to reach wrap completion state without mint succeeding
state_transition_violation.analysis: ZERC20_TOKEN.mint() is called before the Wrapped event emission at line 276. If mint() fails (e.g., due to ValueTooLarge from _update), the entire transaction reverts, preventing partial state.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS by repeated wrap calls with dust amounts
resource_exhaustion.analysis: ZeroAmount check at line 250 prevents zero-amount calls. Each wrap has O(1) gas complexity. nonReentrant modifier at line 103 prevents reentrancy-based DoS. No unbounded loops exist.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Silent failure during wrap leading to lost funds
faulty_error_handling.analysis: All failure paths use explicit revert: ZeroAmount(), ZeroReceiver(), InvalidMsgValue(), UnderlyingPullFailed(). SafeERC20 reverts on transfer failure. No silent failures possible.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Front-run wrap to manipulate reward calculation
race_conditions.analysis: Reward is calculated using pre-deposit liquidity (balanceBefore at line 255). A front-running wrap would affect the reward of a victim but within expected incentive curve behavior. nonReentrant prevents reentrancy. This is expected MEV behavior, not a bug.

counterexample.scenario: Attacker attempts to receive zERC20 without depositing underlying
preconditions: Attacker has approval but insufficient underlying balance
attack_steps: Call wrap() with amount > actual balance
safeTransferFrom reverts due to insufficient balance
counterexample.expected_result: Attack fails - atomicity maintained

audit_results.verification_notes: Atomicity is guaranteed by EVM transaction semantics. All operations either complete together or revert together. VERIFIED: No partial state is possible.

audit_results.title: Unwrap requires sufficient zERC20 balance

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Attempt unwrap with amount > zERC20 balance
input_validation_bypass.analysis: ZERC20_TOKEN.burn(msg.sender, amount) at line 288 calls zERC20.burn() which calls _burn(). OpenZeppelin's _burn() at ERC20Upgradeable._update() reverts with ERC20InsufficientBalance if amount > balance. No pre-check needed - handled by ERC20.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Extract underlying without burning zERC20
state_transition_violation.analysis: burn() at line 288 MUST succeed before transfer at lines 291-296. Order is: burn first, transfer second. If burn fails, revert occurs and no transfer happens.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS by repeated failed unwrap attempts
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Failed unwraps revert immediately on burn failure. Gas cost is borne by attacker. No state pollution from failed attempts. nonReentrant prevents callback exploitation.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Unwrap fails silently without returning tokens
faulty_error_handling.analysis: All failure paths revert: ZeroAmount(), ZeroReceiver(), ERC20 burn revert, InsufficientLiquidity(), UnderlyingSendFailed(). No silent failures.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Race condition between balance check and burn
race_conditions.analysis: There is no separate balance check before burn. The burn operation itself is atomic and checks balance internally via OpenZeppelin ERC20._update(). No TOCTOU vulnerability.

counterexample.scenario: User attempts unwrap with more zERC20 than they hold
counterexample.expected_result: Transaction reverts - no underlying transferred

audit_results.verification_notes: Balance validation is implicit in OpenZeppelin ERC20._update(). Order of operations (burn first, transfer second) prevents extraction without burning.

audit_results.title: Fee calculation uses ceiling rounding

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Manipulate inputs to produce zero fee when fee should be charged
input_validation_bypass.analysis: quoteUnwrapFee() delegates to _rawUnwrapFee() which uses _ceilDiv() at line 278 for ceiling division. The _ceilDiv function at lines 281-285 correctly computes ceil(a/b) = (a + b - 1) / b via q + (r == 0 ? 0 : 1) pattern.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Fee calculation inconsistent between quote and execution
state_transition_violation.analysis: _quoteUnwrapFee(amount, $) at line 285 uses the same IncentiveLib.quoteUnwrapFee() as the public quoteUnwrapFee() view function. Same code path ensures consistency.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Cause overflow in fee calculation
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Overflow protection via: (1) MAX_TARGET_LIQUIDITY = type(uint128).max at line 132, (2) k validation at lines 184-191 ensures k <= maxK, (3) targetLiquidity validation. Intermediate squares are bounded by uint256.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Fee calculation silently returns wrong value
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Edge cases handled: amount == 0 returns 0, T == 0 returns 0, L == 0 returns 0, L > T uses capped values. All branches return explicit values. No silent errors.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Fee params change between quote and unwrap
race_conditions.analysis: setFeeParams() is FEE_MANAGER_ROLE restricted. If params change between user's quote view and unwrap execution, the unwrap uses new params. This is expected admin behavior. Users can use unwrapWithMinOut() with slippage protection.

counterexample.scenario: Attacker tries to pay less fee than expected via rounding manipulation
attack_steps: Call unwrap with amount that produces fractional fee
counterexample.expected_result: Ceiling rounding ensures protocol never undercollects

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: Line 278 uses _ceilDiv for fee calculation. Line 232 uses floor division for rewards. Asymmetric rounding protects protocol (ceil for fees, floor for rewards).

audit_results.title: Burn requires authorized minter

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Call zERC20.burn() from unauthorized address
input_validation_bypass.analysis: burn() function at line 193-196 checks `if (msg.sender != minter()) revert OnlyMinter()` at line 194. This check is the first operation, preventing any unauthorized burn.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Burn tokens when minter is not set
state_transition_violation.analysis: setMinter() at line 177 allows setting minter to address(0). If minter == address(0), burn() would require msg.sender == address(0) which is impossible. Thus, if minter is unset, no burns are possible.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS minting/burning by repeated calls
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Only authorized minter can call burn(). Unauthorized calls revert immediately with minimal gas cost. No DoS vector for legitimate operations.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Burn fails silently without destroying tokens
faulty_error_handling.analysis: OnlyMinter() reverts on unauthorized calls. _burn() from OpenZeppelin reverts on insufficient balance. No silent failures.

race_conditions.attack_vector: setMinter during pending burn transaction
race_conditions.analysis: setMinter() is onlyOwner. If owner changes minter while a burn is pending, the burn will revert with OnlyMinter(). This is expected owner authority behavior, per trust model.

counterexample.scenario: Attacker attempts to burn victim's tokens
counterexample.expected_result: Attack fails - only minter can burn

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: Line 194 enforces minter authorization. Authorization cannot be bypassed.

audit_results.title: Transfer underlying sends correct (amount - fee) to user

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Manipulate fee to receive more underlying than entitled
input_validation_bypass.analysis: amountOut = amount - feeAmount at line 286. Fee is computed from IncentiveLib which uses ceiling division. amountOut is exactly amount minus the computed fee. Transfer at lines 291-296 sends exactly amountOut.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Transfer more than available liquidity
state_transition_violation.analysis: Explicit check at line 291/295: if balance < amountOut, revert InsufficientLiquidity(). This prevents sending more than contract holds. However, NOTE: burn happens first at line 288, so user's zERC20 is burned even if liquidity check fails. This could be a potential issue.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Drain all liquidity via unwrap
resource_exhaustion.analysis: InsufficientLiquidity check at lines 291/295 prevents transfer if balance < amountOut. The fee calculation via IncentiveLib handles low liquidity by increasing fees. amountOut can become very small or zero in extreme cases but transaction completes.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Transfer fails but fee state updated
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Order is: burn (288) -> liquidity check (291/295) -> transfer (292-296) -> feeSurplus update (299). If transfer fails at line 292-293 with UnderlyingSendFailed, transaction reverts, feeSurplus is NOT updated. But if InsufficientLiquidity at 291/295 reverts, burn has already happened. POTENTIAL ISSUE: burn should perhaps be after liquidity check.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Liquidity drained between fee quote and unwrap
race_conditions.analysis: Fee is computed fresh at line 285. Liquidity check is at lines 291/295. If liquidity is drained between user's view call and execution, InsufficientLiquidity could revert. Users should use unwrapWithMinOut for protection.

counterexample.scenario: User unwraps but liquidity insufficient after burn
counterexample.expected_result: Entire transaction reverts - burn is undone
counterexample.actual_result: Transaction reverts, burn is rolled back by EVM

audit_results.verification_notes: The burn-before-transfer ordering is actually safe because EVM transaction semantics ensure all state changes revert on any failure. InsufficientLiquidity check placement is fine. amountOut calculation is correct: amount - fee.

audit_results.title: Unwrap atomicity of burn+transfer operations

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Trigger partial unwrap state (burn without transfer)
input_validation_bypass.analysis: All operations (burn at 288, transfer at 291-296, feeSurplus update at 299) are in single transaction. Any revert rolls back all state changes per EVM semantics. nonReentrant prevents callback exploitation.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Complete unwrap without all operations succeeding
state_transition_violation.analysis: Event Unwrapped at line 301 is emitted only at the end after: burn (288), conditional transfer (289-297), feeSurplus update (299). If any operation fails, revert occurs before event emission.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS unwrap via callback during transfer
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Native transfer uses low-level call at line 292. nonReentrant modifier prevents reentry. Callback to receiver cannot re-enter _unwrap. Receiver can consume gas but that's their cost.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Silent partial unwrap on transfer failure
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Native: if (!success) revert UnderlyingSendFailed() at line 293. ERC20: safeTransfer at line 296 reverts on failure. No silent failures.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Reentrancy during unwrap to manipulate state
race_conditions.analysis: nonReentrant modifier from OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuardTransient prevents any reentry. Lock is set at function entry, cleared at function exit. No bypass possible.

counterexample.scenario: Attacker deploys malicious receiver contract to break atomicity
preconditions: Attacker deploys contract that reverts on receive
attack_steps: Attacker calls unwrap with malicious contract as receiver
counterexample.expected_result: Atomicity maintained - all or nothing

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: nonReentrant modifier at line 126 plus EVM transaction semantics guarantee atomicity. All state changes revert together on any failure.

audit_results.title: Low liquidity triggers high fee via incentive curve

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Bypass fee increase when liquidity is low
input_validation_bypass.analysis: quoteUnwrapFee() at lines 162-177 computes fee based on liquidity. When amount > L (insufficient liquidity case at line 169-176), fee = amount - liquidityMinusFee, which can approach the full amount. Fee increases as liquidity decreases per curve formula.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Unwrap fails when it should succeed with high fee
state_transition_violation.analysis: Unwrap does NOT revert on low liquidity per design. IncentiveLib handles low liquidity by computing high fee, reducing amountOut. The InsufficientLiquidity check at lines 291/295 is for actual balance vs amountOut, not for liquidity threshold. If fee is 100%, amountOut = 0 and no transfer occurs (line 289 check).

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Drain liquidity to force 100% fees on others
resource_exhaustion.analysis: This is expected incentive curve behavior, not an attack. As liquidity decreases, fees increase, discouraging further withdrawals. System is self-stabilizing. Users can check quoteUnwrapFee() before committing.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Fee calculation returns wrong value at boundary
faulty_error_handling.analysis: When amount > L (line 169), fee = amount - max(L - fee_curve, 0) per lines 174-175. If L == 0 (line 247), returns 0 fee which seems wrong for empty pool. However, this edge case means pool is already empty, unwrap would fail anyway.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Liquidity changes between fee quote and execution
race_conditions.analysis: Fee is computed fresh at execution time (line 285), not at quote time. If liquidity changes, execution fee reflects current state. Users should use unwrapWithMinOut for protection.

counterexample.scenario: Pool has low liquidity, user unwraps
attack_steps: User calls quoteUnwrapFee(50) - returns high fee due to low liquidity
User decides to proceed with unwrap
Fee is deducted, amountOut is small
Unwrap succeeds but with reduced output
counterexample.expected_result: High fee charged, user receives reduced output
counterexample.actual_result: Works as designed - incentive curve protects liquidity

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: Per design doc and code, unwrap does NOT revert on low liquidity. Instead, fee increases via incentive curve. Edge case: if L==0, fee returns 0, but pool is empty so transfer would fail anyway.

audit_results.title: Transfer requires sufficient sender balance

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Transfer more tokens than sender holds
input_validation_bypass.analysis: zERC20 inherits from OFTCoreUpgradeable -> ERC20Upgradeable. The _update function at line 153 calls super._update() at line 155 which is OpenZeppelin's ERC20Upgradeable._update(). This function has: require(fromBalance >= value) with ERC20InsufficientBalance revert.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Modify balance without going through _update
state_transition_violation.analysis: All balance modifications (transfer, mint, burn) go through _update override at line 153. There's no alternative path to modify balances. The override ensures hash chain is updated for every balance change.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS transfer by spamming failed transfers
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Failed transfers revert early at OpenZeppelin ERC20._update() balance check. Gas cost is borne by attacker. No state pollution from failed transfers.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Transfer fails silently without proper error
faulty_error_handling.analysis: OpenZeppelin ERC20 uses custom error ERC20InsufficientBalance(sender, balance, value). zERC20._update uses ValueTooLarge at line 154. Both are explicit reverts.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Balance changes between allowance check and transfer
race_conditions.analysis: ERC20 transferFrom uses atomic _spendAllowance and _transfer in same transaction. Balance and allowance are checked/updated atomically. No TOCTOU vulnerability.

counterexample.scenario: User attempts transfer with insufficient balance
counterexample.expected_result: Transfer fails with clear error

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: OpenZeppelin ERC20 balance check is inherited. zERC20._update override does not bypass this check - it calls super._update() which enforces balance requirements.

audit_results.title: BN254 field constraint enforcement (value <= 2^248-1)

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Transfer value exceeding 248-bit limit
input_validation_bypass.analysis: At line 154: `if (value > type(uint248).max) revert ValueTooLarge()`. This check is in _update which is called for ALL token operations (transfer, mint, burn). type(uint248).max = 2^248 - 1. Uses strict > comparison.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Accumulate balance exceeding 248-bit limit via multiple transfers
state_transition_violation.analysis: CRITICAL GAP: The check at line 154 validates `value` (the transfer amount), NOT the resulting balance `balanceOf(to)`. A user could accumulate balance exceeding 2^248-1 through multiple transfers each under the limit. This needs verification.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS by creating tokens that break ZK circuit
resource_exhaustion.analysis: If the balance check gap exists, an attacker could create a balance > 2^248-1 which would be unprovable in the ZK circuit. This would effectively lock those tokens from the privacy system.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: ValueTooLarge check bypassed via overflow
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Solidity 0.8.33 has built-in overflow protection. value > type(uint248).max uses uint256 comparison, no overflow possible. Check is correct.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Concurrent transfers to same address exceeding limit
race_conditions.analysis: Each transfer is atomic. Multiple transactions cannot be processed simultaneously in EVM. However, if value check is on transfer amount not resulting balance, multiple sequential transfers could accumulate past limit.

counterexample.scenario: User accumulates balance > 2^248-1 via multiple transfers
attack_steps: Alice transfers 2^247 to Charlie (value check passes)
Bob transfers 2^247 to Charlie (value check passes)
Charlie now has 2^248 which exceeds 2^248-1 limit
counterexample.expected_result: Second transfer should fail if balance check exists
counterexample.actual_result: UNKNOWN - needs code verification whether balance or value is checked

audit_results.verification_notes: CRITICAL: Line 154 checks `value` not `balanceOf(to) + value`. If only transfer value is validated, accumulated balances could exceed 2^248-1, breaking ZK circuit compatibility. This is flagged as potential vulnerability requiring manual verification of whether resulting balance should be checked.

audit_results.title: Balance update maintains conservation of value

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Manipulate balance update to create tokens from nothing
input_validation_bypass.analysis: super._update() at line 155 calls OpenZeppelin ERC20Upgradeable._update() which does: (1) for transfers: from_balance -= value, to_balance += value, (2) for mint: to_balance += value, totalSupply += value, (3) for burn: from_balance -= value, totalSupply -= value. All arithmetic is checked (Solidity 0.8+).

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Create tokens without increasing totalSupply
state_transition_violation.analysis: mint() at 185-188 calls _mint() which calls _update(address(0), to, value) incrementing totalSupply. teleport() at 146-147 calls _mint() same way. No path creates balance without totalSupply increase.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Overflow totalSupply
resource_exhaustion.analysis: OpenZeppelin ERC20._update uses unchecked{} for performance but totalSupply is bounded by sum of all mints. With value <= 2^248-1 per transfer and finite transactions, overflow is impractical. Solidity 0.8 overflow protection applies to checked arithmetic elsewhere.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Balance update fails silently
faulty_error_handling.analysis: OpenZeppelin ERC20._update has explicit error handling: ERC20InsufficientBalance, ERC20InvalidSender, ERC20InvalidReceiver. No silent failures.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Concurrent balance updates causing inconsistency
race_conditions.analysis: EVM executes transactions sequentially. Each _update is atomic. No race conditions possible at smart contract level.

counterexample.scenario: Verify conservation: sum(balances) == totalSupply
attack_steps: User A transfers 100 to User B
counterexample.expected_result: Conservation maintained
counterexample.actual_result: Conservation maintained - OpenZeppelin ERC20 is well-audited

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: OpenZeppelin ERC20Upgradeable is battle-tested. Conservation invariant: totalSupply = sum(balances) is maintained by _update implementation.

audit_results.title: Hash chain uses SHA-256 with 248-bit truncation

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Bypass hash chain update during transfer
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Hash chain update at line 157 is in _update override. Every balance change (transfer, mint, burn) calls _update. The hash chain update is unconditional within _update after super._update() succeeds.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Hash chain uses wrong hash function
state_transition_violation.analysis: Line 8 explicitly uses sha256(). Line 9 masks with 0x00FF...FF (248 bits). This matches specification: SHA-256 truncated to 248 bits. Not keccak256.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS by expensive hash computation
resource_exhaustion.analysis: sha256 is a precompile (address 0x02) with fixed gas cost. Input is fixed size: 32 + 20 + 20 + 32 = 104 bytes. Gas cost is predictable and bounded.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Hash computation produces wrong result on edge inputs
faulty_error_handling.analysis: abi.encodePacked(prev, from, to, value) produces deterministic byte sequence. sha256 precompile is cryptographically sound. Masking with & 0x00FF...FF is bitwise AND, deterministic.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Hash chain fork via concurrent updates
race_conditions.analysis: EVM transactions are sequential. Hash chain update reads $.hashChain, computes new value, writes back atomically within transaction. No forks possible.

counterexample.scenario: Verify hash chain computation matches specification
counterexample.expected_result: On-chain hash matches ZK circuit hash

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: ShaHashChainLib uses sha256() not keccak256(). 248-bit truncation via bitmask. Encoding uses abi.encodePacked. Cross-verification with ZK circuit needed for full assurance.

audit_results.title: IndexedTransfer events emit monotonic indices

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Manipulate index value in event
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Line 158: `emit IndexedTransfer($.index++, from, to, value)`. The index is read from storage, used in event, then incremented. Post-increment (index++) ensures the emitted value is current index, then storage is incremented for next transfer.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Reset or manipulate index storage
state_transition_violation.analysis: index() at line 82-84 is a public view returning $.index. There is NO setter function for index. The only modification is $.index++ at line 158. Index cannot be reset or decremented.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Overflow index counter
resource_exhaustion.analysis: $.index is uint256. With one increment per transfer, overflow requires 2^256 transfers which is computationally impossible in the lifetime of the universe.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Index increment fails silently
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Post-increment is a simple uint256++ with Solidity 0.8 overflow protection (which won't trigger given above analysis). Operation cannot fail.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Concurrent transfers get same index
race_conditions.analysis: EVM executes transactions sequentially. Each _update reads current $.index, emits event, increments. Next transaction sees incremented value. No duplicate indices possible.

counterexample.scenario: Verify index monotonicity across transfers
attack_steps: Transfer 1: emits IndexedTransfer with index 100, storage becomes 101
Transfer 2: emits IndexedTransfer with index 101, storage becomes 102
Transfer 3: emits IndexedTransfer with index 102, storage becomes 103
counterexample.expected_result: Strictly monotonically increasing indices

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: Line 158 uses $.index++ which guarantees monotonic increase. No reset mechanism exists. Index is strictly increasing by 1 for each transfer.

audit_results.title: Transfer completion atomicity (balance, hash chain, event)

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Complete transfer without all operations succeeding
input_validation_bypass.analysis: _update at lines 153-159 performs: (1) value check line 154, (2) balance update via super._update() line 155, (3) hash chain update line 157, (4) event emission line 158. All in single function call within single transaction.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Balance updated but hash chain not updated
state_transition_violation.analysis: super._update() at line 155 executes first. If it reverts, hash chain update at line 157 never executes. If super._update() succeeds, hash chain update is next and cannot be skipped. Sequence is atomic.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS transfer by reverting in _afterTokenTransfer hook
resource_exhaustion.analysis: zERC20 overrides _update, not _afterTokenTransfer. The hook pattern is: _beforeTokenTransfer -> balance update -> _afterTokenTransfer. zERC20 uses _update override instead, which wraps super._update() with pre/post logic. This is safer pattern.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Partial transfer state on hash chain computation error
faulty_error_handling.analysis: ShaHashChainLib.compute() is pure computation using sha256 precompile. Cannot fail under normal conditions. If it somehow failed (out of gas), entire transaction reverts including balance update.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Reentrancy to manipulate transfer state
race_conditions.analysis: zERC20 inherits from ERC20Upgradeable which doesn't have hooks that could be exploited for reentrancy. _update completes atomically. No external calls between balance update and hash chain update.

counterexample.scenario: Verify all operations complete together or none complete
counterexample.expected_result: Atomicity maintained

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: _update override at lines 153-159 ensures all operations (value check, balance update, hash chain, event) execute atomically. No partial state is possible.

audit_results.title: Transfer rejection precision at MAX_VALUE boundary

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Transfer exactly at MAX_VALUE passes incorrectly
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Line 154: `if (value > type(uint248).max) revert ValueTooLarge()`. Uses strict > comparison. type(uint248).max = 2^248 - 1. Value exactly equal to 2^248 - 1 does NOT trigger revert (correct). Value equal to 2^248 triggers revert (correct).

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Valid transfer incorrectly rejected at boundary
state_transition_violation.analysis: Boundary analysis: value = 2^248 - 1 -> condition false -> no revert (correct). value = 2^248 -> condition true -> revert (correct). No false positives at boundary.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Generate many ValueTooLarge errors
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Reverts consume gas but don't pollute state. Attacker pays for failed transactions. No DoS vector.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: ValueTooLarge revert missing or unclear
faulty_error_handling.analysis: ValueTooLarge error defined at line 52. Used at line 154. Custom error with no parameters - clear but could be more informative (include the actual value). Design choice, not vulnerability.

race_conditions.attack_vector: MAX_VALUE changes during transaction
race_conditions.analysis: type(uint248).max is a compile-time constant. Cannot change at runtime. No race condition possible.

counterexample.scenario: Boundary test for MAX_VALUE
attack_steps: Transfer value = MAX_VALUE: passes (value > MAX_VALUE is false)
Transfer value = MAX_VALUE + 1: fails (value > MAX_VALUE is true)
counterexample.expected_result: Precise boundary enforcement

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: Line 154 uses strict > comparison. Transfers at exactly MAX_VALUE succeed, transfers exceeding MAX_VALUE fail. Boundary is precise.

audit_results.title: Verifier contract stateless and always ready

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Lock Verifier in blocked state
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Verifier inherits PausableUpgradeable. Functions marked whenNotPaused (lines 265, 311, 341, 392) can be blocked by pause. Pause is triggered by: (1) emergency via conflicting proofs at line 285, (2) admin activateEmergency() at line 458. Both are controlled scenarios.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Verifier enters state that blocks operations permanently
state_transition_violation.analysis: Emergency pause can be deactivated by owner via deactivateEmergency() at line 464. Recovery path exists. However, if owner key is lost, Verifier is permanently paused. This is expected trust model for owner role.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Fill up storage mappings to DoS
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Mappings (reservedHashChains, provedTransferRoots, globalTransferRoots, totalTeleported) are keyed by uint64 index or uint256 recipient. Storage is gas-paid by caller. No free storage consumption attack.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Silent failure leaves Verifier in bad state
faulty_error_handling.analysis: All functions use explicit require/revert with custom errors. No silent failures. Failed operations revert cleanly without state corruption.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Concurrent operations cause state inconsistency
race_conditions.analysis: EVM executes transactions sequentially. Verifier doesn't have reentrancy issues - no external calls before state updates in critical paths. Storage updates are atomic.

counterexample.scenario: Attempt to lock Verifier via malicious proof
preconditions: Attacker submits first valid proof for index N
attack_steps: Attacker submits second proof for same index N with different root
Check at line 283: existingRoot != 0 && existingRoot != newRoot
counterexample.expected_result: Emergency mode is intentional safety mechanism
counterexample.actual_result: Emergency triggered as designed - indicates ZK system bug

audit_results.verification_notes: Verifier CAN be paused via emergency mechanism (conflicting proofs) or owner action. This is by design. Recovery via deactivateEmergency() exists. Only concern is owner key loss which is out of scope per trust model.

audit_results.title: Hash chain checkpoint immutable once reserved

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Overwrite existing reserved hash chain
input_validation_bypass.analysis: reserveHashChain() at lines 251-260 unconditionally writes: `$.reservedHashChains[index_] = hashChain_` at line 256. There is NO check whether slot is already occupied. POTENTIAL ISSUE: Existing reservations can be overwritten.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Modify reserved checkpoint after proof submission
state_transition_violation.analysis: If a reservation exists at index N and proveTransferRoot uses it, then someone calls reserveHashChain when index_ equals N again (if index hasn't advanced), the reservation is overwritten. However, index_ comes from tokenContract.index() which is monotonically increasing. Same index can only be reserved if no transfers happened since last reservation.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Reserve many indices to fill storage
resource_exhaustion.analysis: reserveHashChain is permissionless (no access control). Anyone can call it to reserve the current index. Each call overwrites the slot for current index. Storage cost is borne by caller. Index advances with transfers, so historical indices become stale.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Reservation fails silently
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Function always succeeds (no reverts). Emits HashChainReserved event. Returns (index, hashChain). No silent failures, but also no validation of whether reservation is meaningful.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Concurrent reservations overwrite each other
race_conditions.analysis: Two reservations at same index in same block would result in last-write-wins. However, both would reserve the same (index, hashChain) pair since zERC20 state is same for both. Overwriting with same value is harmless.

counterexample.scenario: Attempt to overwrite existing reservation with different value
preconditions: Index N reserved with hashChain A
attack_steps: Overwrite with same value - no attack
counterexample.expected_result: Same index reservation yields same value
counterexample.actual_result: Overwrite only possible with same value

audit_results.verification_notes: Reservation CAN be overwritten but only with same value (since zERC20 index is monotonic and hashChain is deterministic). If transfers occur between reservations, new index is different so different slot used. VERIFIED: No actual vulnerability due to deterministic nature of index and hashChain.

audit_results.title: HashChainReserved event consistency with storage

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Event emitted without storage write
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Order at lines 256-258: (1) storage write at 256, (2) latestReservedIndex update at 257, (3) event emission at 258. Event is emitted AFTER both storage operations. Cannot emit event without storage update.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Event data doesn't match stored data
state_transition_violation.analysis: Event at line 258: `emit HashChainReserved(index_, hashChain_)`. Storage at line 256: `$.reservedHashChains[index_] = hashChain_`. Same variables used for both. Data matches.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Emit many events to burden indexers
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Events are paid by gas. Each reserveHashChain call costs caller gas. No amplification attack. Log storage is chain-level, not contract-level.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Storage succeeds but event fails
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Event emission cannot fail in Solidity. emit is a log opcode that always succeeds if transaction has enough gas. If out of gas, entire transaction reverts including storage.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Storage and event have different values due to race
race_conditions.analysis: index_ and hashChain_ are local variables set at lines 254-255. They cannot change between storage write and event emission within same transaction.

counterexample.scenario: Verify event-storage consistency
attack_steps: Event and storage both have index=100, hashChain=0xABC...
counterexample.expected_result: Event data matches storage

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: Lines 256-258 show storage write before event emission using same local variables. Event-storage consistency is guaranteed.

audit_results.title: Transfer root proof requires prior hash chain reservation

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Submit proof without prior reservation
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Lines 279-281: `uint256 expectedHashChain = $.reservedHashChains[newIndex]; require(expectedHashChain != 0, ReserveHashChainNotFound(newIndex));`. Proof submission requires non-zero reservation at the target index.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Proof accepted for unreserved index
state_transition_violation.analysis: newIndex is extracted from proof at line 270. Reservation check uses this index. If reservedHashChains[newIndex] == 0, ReserveHashChainNotFound reverts. Proof cannot be accepted without reservation.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS by consuming all reservations
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Reservations are keyed by zERC20 index which is monotonically increasing. Each index can only have one reservation. Consuming reservations requires legitimate transfers to advance index. No amplification attack.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Proof submission fails silently on missing reservation
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Explicit revert with ReserveHashChainNotFound(newIndex) at line 280. Not silent - provides clear error with the missing index.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Reservation deleted between check and use
race_conditions.analysis: Reservations cannot be deleted - no delete function exists. Reservations can be overwritten but only with same value (per previous analysis). Check and use are in same transaction, atomic.

counterexample.scenario: Attempt to prove root without reservation
preconditions: Attacker has valid proof for index 50
counterexample.expected_result: Proof rejected due to missing reservation

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: Lines 279-280 require reservation to exist (non-zero) before proof can be accepted. Missing reservation causes explicit revert.

audit_results.title: Nova proof validation uses correct public inputs

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Submit proof with manipulated public inputs
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Proof is decoded at line 266. Public inputs extracted at lines 267-272. These are passed to verifyOpaqueNovaProof at line 274. The ZK verifier checks that proof is valid for these exact inputs. Manipulation of inputs invalidates the proof.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Proof verified against wrong public inputs
state_transition_violation.analysis: After verification at line 274, additional checks at lines 275-281 ensure: (1) oldRoot matches stored provedTransferRoots[oldIndex], (2) newHashChain matches reservedHashChains[newIndex]. Public inputs are cross-validated against on-chain state.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS via expensive proof verification
resource_exhaustion.analysis: verifyOpaqueNovaProof is external call to IRootDecider. Verification cost depends on ZK circuit complexity. Gas is bounded by block limit. Caller pays for verification. No amplification.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Invalid proof silently accepted
faulty_error_handling.analysis: require(IRootDecider($.rootDecider).verifyOpaqueNovaProof(proof_), InvalidProof()). If verification returns false, InvalidProof error is thrown. No silent acceptance.

race_conditions.attack_vector: rootDecider changed during proof verification
race_conditions.analysis: setVerifiers() at lines 475-502 is onlyOwner. If owner changes rootDecider during proof verification transaction, verification uses the rootDecider at time of call. Atomic read at line 274. Owner action is out of scope.

counterexample.scenario: Attempt to use proof with wrong public inputs
preconditions: Attacker has valid proof for (oldIndex=10, newIndex=20, newRoot=A)
Attacker modifies proof to claim newRoot=B
attack_steps: verifyOpaqueNovaProof checks proof against public inputs including newRoot=B
ZK verification fails because proof was generated for newRoot=A
counterexample.expected_result: Modified proof rejected

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: Lines 274-281 perform both ZK verification and cross-validation against on-chain state. Public inputs are bound to proof by ZK soundness, and additionally validated against storage.

audit_results.title: STATE-TRANSFER-ROOT-PROVED only after valid ZKP verification

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Store root without proof verification
input_validation_bypass.analysis: provedTransferRoots write at line 289: `$.provedTransferRoots[newIndex] = newRoot`. This is AFTER require at line 274 which calls verifyOpaqueNovaProof. Also after require at line 280 for reservation check. No bypass path exists.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Admin function to set proved roots
state_transition_violation.analysis: Searched for all writes to provedTransferRoots. Found: (1) line 237 in initializer sets provedTransferRoots[0] = INITIAL_TRANSFER_ROOT, (2) line 289 in proveTransferRoot. No admin setter exists. Only paths are initialization and proof verification.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Fill provedTransferRoots mapping
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Each root storage requires valid ZK proof which requires computational resources to generate. No free storage. Mapping is keyed by uint64 index. Storage cost paid by caller.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Root stored on verification failure
faulty_error_handling.analysis: require at line 274 reverts on verification failure. Line 289 root storage is only reached if require passes. Order is enforced by sequential execution. No error path leads to storage.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Root stored twice with different values
race_conditions.analysis: Lines 282-288 handle case where root already exists at index. If existingRoot != 0 && existingRoot != newRoot, emergency is triggered and function returns early. No overwrite with different value. Same value can be written (idempotent).

counterexample.scenario: Attempt to store root without valid proof
counterexample.expected_result: Invalid proof rejected, no root stored

audit_results.verification_notes: VERIFIED: provedTransferRoots can only be written via: (1) initializer with constant INITIAL_TRANSFER_ROOT, or (2) proveTransferRoot after successful ZK verification. No bypass exists.

key_findings.summary: BN254 value constraint checks transfer value, not resulting balance
key_findings.detail: Line 154 in zERC20._update checks 'value > type(uint248).max' but does NOT check 'balanceOf(to) + value > type(uint248).max'. This means accumulated balances could theoretically exceed 2^248-1 through multiple transfers, potentially breaking ZK circuit compatibility. Requires verification of whether this is intentional design or a gap.
key_findings.recommendation: Verify if check should be on resulting balance (balanceOf(to) + value for mints/transfers) rather than just transfer value. If gap confirmed, add balance validation.

IncentiveLib ceiling division for fees, floor division for rewards
OpenZeppelin ERC20 balance checks inherited by zERC20
